parts.label: a
parts.technique: Angle between two vectors/lines using scalar product
parts.reason: The explicit 'concepts no statement covers' list excludes scalar (dot) product, including the angle between vectors or lines; this part requires exactly that.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Showing a point lies on a vector line r=a+λb
parts.reason: This requires substituting into the vector equation of a line and solving for λ to confirm a point lies on it; 'vector equation of a line (r=a+λb)' is explicitly listed among concepts no statement covers, so this technique (not mere position-vector arithmetic) is out of spec.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Intersection of two lines given in vector form
parts.reason: 'Intersection of lines' is explicitly listed among concepts no statement covers.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Distance between two points (using intersection point X)
parts.reason: Although magnitude/distance between position vectors is ordinary in-spec vector work (P10.4), this part depends entirely on X, the answer to part (c) which is out of spec (intersection of lines); per the rule that a part relying on an out-of-spec answer is OUT, this part is OUT.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Area of triangle using vector-derived angle and length
parts.reason: Depends on the angle from part (a) and length from part (d), both out-of-spec (dot-product angle and intersection-dependent distance), so this part is OUT.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Finding points on a vector line using λ from distance condition
parts.reason: Requires substituting into the vector equation of line l2 (r=a+λb) and depends on prior out-of-spec results (X, AX); vector equation of a line is explicitly excluded and this part relies on earlier out-of-spec parts.
